events.title: Cornyn elected
events.text: John Cornyn won the U.S. Senate seat that is open in 2026.

events.title: Republicans take the House
events.text: Republicans won the Texas House, 88 seats to 62, their first majority there since Reconstruction; they had held the state Senate since 1996.

events.title: Paxton in the House
events.text: Ken Paxton began ten years in the Texas House.

events.title: A 23-point margin
events.text: Texas voted Republican for president by almost twenty-three points, as it had in every election since 1980.

events.title: The margin narrows
events.text: Texas still voted Republican for president, but by under twelve points.

events.title: A sixth-grade teacher
events.text: James Talarico, a University of Texas graduate, began teaching sixth grade in San Antonio.

events.title: Paxton in the Senate
events.text: Paxton moved to the Texas Senate, where he served until 2015.

events.title: Attorney general
events.text: Paxton was elected attorney general; he took office in January 2015.

events.title: Securities indictment
events.text: Paxton was indicted on state securities-fraud charges and pleaded not guilty.

events.title: Single digits
events.text: Donald Trump carried Texas by nine points over Hillary Clinton.

events.title: Cruz re-elected
events.text: Ted Cruz beat Beto O'Rourke, 50.9 to 48.3 percent.

events.title: Tarrant turns
events.text: O'Rourke carried Tarrant County, the first statewide Democrat to do so since 1994.

events.title: Youngest member
events.text: Talarico was elected to the Texas House from Round Rock at twenty-nine, its youngest member.

events.title: Aides go to the FBI
events.text: Eight of Paxton's senior aides reported him to the FBI, alleging bribery and abuse of office to help a donor.

events.title: Texas v. Pennsylvania
events.text: The U.S. Supreme Court rejected Paxton's suit to overturn the presidential results in four states, for lack of standing.

events.title: Starr County shifts
events.text: Starr County, which gave O'Rourke 77 percent in 2018, gave Donald Trump 47 percent.

events.title: A 5.6-point race
events.text: Donald Trump carried Texas by 5.6 points over Joe Biden.

events.title: Insulin cap
events.text: A state law capped insulin co-pays at $25; Talarico, who has Type 1 diabetes, was a co-lead on the bill.

events.title: “God is nonbinary”
events.text: In a House debate on school sports, Talarico said “God is nonbinary”; he later called the remark deliberately provocative.

events.title: Quorum break
events.text: Talarico joined House Democrats who left the state, denying the House a quorum.

events.title: Paxton re-elected
events.text: Paxton won a third term as attorney general.

events.title: Impeached
events.text: On 27 May the Republican-led Texas House impeached Paxton, 121 to 23, on 20 articles.

events.title: Acquitted
events.text: On 16 September the Texas Senate acquitted Paxton on all 16 articles it tried.

events.title: Restitution deal
events.text: Paxton agreed to pay about $300,000 in restitution in the securities case, without admitting wrongdoing.

events.title: Starr votes Republican
events.text: Starr County voted Republican for president for the first time since 1892.

events.title: Webb County flips
events.text: Webb County, home to Laredo, gave a Republican presidential candidate a majority for the first time since 1912.

events.title: Split tickets
events.text: Donald Trump carried Hidalgo County for president while Colin Allred, a Democrat, carried it for the Senate.

events.title: Cruz re-elected
events.text: Ted Cruz beat Colin Allred, 53.1 to 44.6 percent; the Libertarian Ted Brown won 267,039 votes.

events.title: Paxton runs
events.text: On 8 April Paxton announced a challenge to Senator John Cornyn in the Republican primary.

events.title: Whistleblower verdict
events.text: A Travis County court awarded four of the whistleblowers $6.6 million; Paxton dropped his appeal in July.

events.title: Case dismissed
events.text: On 18 June the securities charges against Paxton were dismissed.

events.title: Ten Commandments debate
events.text: Talarico's argument against a bill to display the Ten Commandments in classrooms drew millions of views.

events.title: Talarico runs
events.text: On 9 September Talarico entered the Democratic primary for the Senate.

events.title: Allred withdraws
events.text: On 8 December Colin Allred left the Democratic Senate primary to run for the U.S. House.

events.title: Primary day
events.text: On 3 March Talarico beat Jasmine Crockett outright; Cornyn led Paxton, but short of a majority.

events.title: Libertarians in Abilene
events.text: The Libertarian state convention in Abilene nominated Ted Brown for the Senate.

events.title: Court declines
events.text: On 15 May the Texas Supreme Court turned down bids by Governor Abbott and Paxton to remove Democrats who broke quorum in 2025.

events.title: Trump endorses Paxton
events.text: On 19 May President Trump endorsed Paxton, a week before the runoff.

events.title: Paxton wins the runoff
events.text: On 26 May Paxton beat Cornyn with 63.8 percent, the first loss by a sitting Texas senator to his own party since 1970.

events.title: A toss-up
events.text: In August the Cook Political Report and Sabato's Crystal Ball rated the race a toss-up.

events.title: Early voting
events.text: In-person early voting runs from 19 to 30 October.

events.title: Election Day
events.text: On 3 November Texans choose between Paxton, Talarico, Brown and four registered write-in candidates.

chartNote: Each state is coloured by the margin of the most recent presidential popular vote (Democratic minus Republican share of all votes; FEC certified results). It is a simplification: Texas elects its senator in its own race, and many Texans split their tickets (in 2024 the Republican presidential margin was about five points larger than the Republican Senate margin), so the presidential colour is a backdrop, not a forecast. Shares are of land area, not of people or votes. Boundaries are today's states (Natural Earth); the map is framed on Texas, so outer states are cut at the edge.
